lawyer:
Abdul Quayum with Maqbul Hossain, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner 
M A Wahhab Miah with Aminul Islam Mondal, Advocates ----- For the Opposite Party No. 1
parties:
Mahbubul Huq (Md) ------ Petitioner
vs
Md A Kader Munshi & Others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Defendant No. 1 as petitioner obtained this Rule challenging the order dated 21-9-1998 passed by Mr Bazlur Rahman, Senior Assistant Judge, Barguna in Title Suit No. 17 of 1998 rejecting an application under Order 7, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

2. Brief facts of the case is that, the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 17 of 1998 in the said Court for declaration that the impugned auction sale described in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint is illegal, void, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff. The plaintiff opposite party No. 1 filed the suit being Title Suit No. 17 of 1998 alleging, in short, inter alia, that the suit property belonged to Bani Amin and Arab Ali, the predecessors who were the recorded tenants of CS khatian, that during the revisional settlement operation the said land was wrongly recorded in the name of Late Wazed Ali Zamaddar, predecessor of the defendant, hence the plaintiff-opposite-party filed Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 before the Assistant Judge, Barguna for declaration of their title in the suit land. It was further stated in the plaint that the said Bani Amin and Arab Ali had their dwelling houses, etc. in the suit land appertaining to PS khatian No. 59 measuring an area of 12.86 but only 0.62 decimals of land was recorded in RS Khatian in the name of Bani Amin. In Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 the present petitioner was a defendant along with his brother Mahabubul Haque and others being the heirs of Late Wazed Ali Zamaddar, the said defendants filed written statements in the said Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 contending, inter alia, that their father Late Wazed Ali auction purchased the suit land in Money Suit No, 5 of 1932, vide Money Execution Case No. 14 of 1933 of the 1st Court of Munsif, Pirojpur and took possession on 20-2-1934 and since then was in possession of the same. The further case of the plaintiff-opposite-party No. 1 is that, the aforesaid Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 was dismissed on contest and he pursued the matter unsuccessfully up to the Appellate Di vision. The further case of the plaintiff-opposite-party No. 1 in the present suit is that, the Bainanama and Dakhalnama vide Exhibits. A and D filed by the defendants in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 in the trial Court were taken back by them on 23-7-86 on application and certified copies of the same were refiled before the High Court Division long after more than 8 years in Civil Revision No. 732 of 1990, filed by the plaintiff opposite party instead of original Exhibits A and B filed and taken back as aforesaid. The plaintiff further alleged that the learned District Judges having not been in seisin of the said Exhibits A and B, could not properly adjudicate the matter. The defendants filed the certified copies of Exhibits. A and B before the High Court Division only on 2-11-94 in said Civil Revision No. 732 of 1990, the High Court Division discharged the Rule vide its judgment and order dated 31-1-95 and the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 thus did not get sufficient time to verify those copies. The plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 further stated in his plaint of the present suit that, after obtaining certified copies of Bainanama and Dakhalnama of the aforesaid Money Suit No. 5 of 1932 and Money Execution Case No. 14 of 1933 on 11-8-97, he found that the certified copies of the Exhibits. A and B filed before the Hon'ble High Court Di vision on 2-11-1994 were forged, fabricated and false and on consideration of the said fake documents, the superior Courts ultimately dismissed his suit. The plaintiff further alleged that after obtaining the certified copies of the Bainanama and Dakhalnama of Money Suit No. 5 of 1932 and Money Execution Case No. 14 of 1933 he came to certified copies before the Appellate Division in a know of the said fraud on 11-8-97 and filed the said separate paper book at the time of hearing of the leave petition, but the Hon'ble Appellate Division has neither referred the said Paper Book nor discussed or gave any findings on those papers in its judgment and order dated 21-8-97 rejecting the Leave Petition. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances the plaintiff-opposite party instituted the present suit as aforesaid.

3. The defendant-petitioner appeared in the, suit and filed an application under Order 7, rule 11(a) and (d) of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejecting the plaint pleading that the suit is barred by limitation and rule of res judicata alleging that, the plaintiff having instituted the present suit for declaration that the Bainanama and Dakhalnami of Money Suit No. 5 of 1932 and Money Execution Case No. 14 of 1933 as described in schedule Ka of the plaint are forged, collusive, ineffective, inoperative, non-existent, baseless and not binding upon the plaintiff is not maintainable in this subsequent suit as it is barred by limitation as well as by their principle of res judicata under section 11 of the Code alleging the, that plaintiff-opposite-party had already instituted Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 on the same facts and the defendant Nos. 3 and 10 of that suit including the petitioner, filed a written statement on 23-7-1986 contesting the suit. The petitioner further alleged in the application that, in the said written statements they stated the case of auction sale in Money Suit No. 5 of 1932 and Money Execution Case No. 14 of 1933 in question and produced the Bainanama and Dakhalnama of the case in the said suit which were duly marked as Exts. A and B at the time of trial and as such the plaintiff 'had clear knowledge of the aforesaid Bainanama and Dakhalnama at least from the date of filing of their written statements, that is, from 23-7- 86, but the present suit having not been filed within 6 years from 23-7-86, the suit is barred by limitation and, as such, the plaint is liable to be rejected.

4. The defendant-petitioner secondly, alleged that, in the former Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 the same facts of the aforesaid auction sale, Bainanama, Dakhalnama, etc. having been decided between the same parties, the present suit having been brought on the same set of facts is barred by rule of res judicata as per provision of section 11 of the Code.

5. The trial Court on hearing the aforesaid application rejected the same vide impugned order dated 21-9-98 as not maintainable. The defendant petitioner being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned order moved this Court under section 115 of the Code and obtained the present Rule.

6. I have perused the application filed by the defendant-petitioner before the trial Court under Order 7, rule 11(a) and (d) of the Code, the judgment passed in Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 by the trial Court, the judgment of the appellate Court, the judgment of the High Court Division passed in Civil Revision No. 732 of 1990 and the judgment of the Appellate Division in the aforesaid Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 322 of 1995 arising out of the said Title suit No. 45 of 1984 enclosed with supple me nary affidavit filed by the defendant petitioner in the case and also heard the learned Advocates of both the sides at length.

7. Mr Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioner, submits that the learned Senior Assistant Judge has committed an error of law in rejecting the application of the petitioner filed under Order 7, rule 11(a) and (d) of the Code in failing to find that the suit was barred by law of limitation and by the principle of res judicata as provided in section 11 of the Code Mr Quayum, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, vehemently pressed for rejection of the plaint on two grounds, firstly, on point of limitation and secondly, as barred by rule of res judicata.

8. Elucidating his first submission Mr. Abdul Quayum submits that, even if we accept that the plaintiff had no knowledge of the spurious Bainanama and Dakhalnama earlier, it can definitely be pleaded that he had definite knowledge of the same at least when the fact of aforesaid auction sale in Money Suit No. 5 of 1932 and Money Execution Case No. 4 of 1933 were disclosed in the written statements filed on 23-7-86 in Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 and were produced in Court and admitted into evidence and marked as Exhibits A and B during trial of the suit in 1986. So, the suit having been filed in 1988 referring the same facts and challenging the said Bainanama and Dakhalnama, the present suit is clearly barred by law of limitation and the trial Court ought to have rejected the plaint. He further submits that the trial Court ought to have found that the plaintiffs claim that, he came to know that Exhibits A and B were forged, false and fabricated documents only on 11-8-97 after obtaining the certified copies of the said documents is not true and correct

9. Mr MA Wahhab Miah, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff opposite party, on the other hand submits that the present suit has been instituted by the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 pleading that the defendant petitioner and other defendants of the earlier suit practiced fraud upon the plaintiff as well as upon the Courts. He further submits that, fraud vitiates everything if the plaintiff IS able to prove the same and the question of limitation takes effect from the date of knowledge of such fraud. In support of his submission Mr M A Wahhab Mia, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite party, has referred to section 18 of the Limitation Act which deals with the effect of fraud. Section 18 of the Limitation Act is quoted before:

"18. Effect of fraud-Where any person having a right to institute a suit or make an application has, by means of fraud, been kept from the knowledge on such right or of the title on which it is founded, or where any document necessary to establish such right has been fraudulently concealed from him, the time limited for instituting a suit or making an application

(a) against the person guilty of the fraud or necessary thereto or

(b) against any person claiming through him otherwise than in good faith and for a valuable consideration,

shall be computed from the time when the fraud first became known to the person injuriously affected thereby, or, in the case of the concealed document, when he first had the means of producing it or compelling its production."

10. Referring to the above, Mr M A Wahhab Mia, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite arty, submits that the Bainanama and Dakhalnama were not filed with the written statements but were produced in Court by the defendant-petitioner and were duly market-Exhibits A and B during hearing of the suit. But the defendant No. 2 of the present suit who was also a defendant in that suit, on an application dated 23-7-86 took back those documents immediately after those were marked exhibits with a condition to refile the same, but were not filed in the appeal. At the time of hearing of the Civil Revision, being Civil Revision No. 732 of 1990, before the High Court Division, the present defendant-petitioner filed certified copies of Exhibits A and B, before the High Court Division by an affidavit on 2-11-94 instead of filing those which were originally marked exhibits by the trial Court. It may be mentioned here that the said Rule was heard on 30-1-95 and disposed of by the High Court Division vide its judgment dated 31-1-95. It is submitted that the petitioner and other defendants of the said suit willfully and deliberately withheld, suppressed and concealed the originals of said Exhibits A and B with a deceitful motive and practiced fraud upon the plaintiff as well as upon the Court. Mr Wahhab continued that, in such a situation the plaintiff-opposite party has no opportunity to verify and ascertain the genuineness of these exhibits. But they became suspicious of the same and obtained certified copies of the said Bainanama and dakhalnama on 11-8-97 and came to know definitely for the first time that, the certified copies of Exhibits. A and B filed before the High Court Division were not the genuine but forged, and then he instituted the present suit being Suit No. 17 of 1998 which is within time of limitation since the plaintiff first came to know of the same on 11-8-97. The learned Advocate further argued that, even if we accept that he had knowledge of the said documents when those were filed in the High Court Division on 2-11-94, then also the suit filed-in 1994 is within time. Therefore, it cannot be pleaded that the suit is barred by limitation. Moreover, the learned Advocate continued, the question of limitation being a mixed question of law and fact this cannot be a ground for rejection of plaint under Order 7, rule 11(d) of the Code before taking evidence. In order to prove and substantiate that the suit is barred by limitation, that must be decided upon framing an issue and taking evidence. In support of his submission the learned Advocate Mr M A Wahhab Miah, submits that, the limitation will be computed in such a suit under section 18 of the Limitation Act from the date when the fraud is detected and proved. He has referred a case of Abdul Khair Mia vs Abdul Latif Sarder, reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167. In the said case our Appellate Division has held with reference to section 18 of the Limitation Act that:

"If fraud is proved then there is no question of limitation and it will run from the date when fraud was detected".

<u>11. Mr M A Wahhab Mia has also referred the case between Naeem Finance Limited & another vs Bashir Ahmed Rafique, Administrator, Muslim Insurance Co Ltd & another, reported in 23 DLR (SC) 81, case between Shahabuddin (Md) and another vs Habibur Rahman and others, reported in 50 DLR (AD) 99, in support of his submission that the question of limitation being a mixed question of law and fact the plaint cannot be rejected on this ground under Order 7, rule 11 (d) of the Code. In the case reported in aforesaid 23 DLR (SC) 81, it has been held that:</u>

<u>"Allegation of fraud to save limitation under section 18, must be clearly made out in the pleading.</u>

<u>The question of fraud is a mixed question of law and fact. If a person wants to take advantage of the provisions of section 18 of the Limitation Act, namely, that due to fraud he could not file his complaint within the time permissible by law, it is necessary that such party should have laid some foundation fo it. In the absence of any pleading to that effect the party concerned cannot be allowed to raise this point in appeal (before the Supreme Court)."</u>

<u>12. Mr M A Wahhab Miah, the learned Advocate, by making specific reference to the averments made by, the plaintiff in the plaint, submits that, the plaintiff-opposite party has specifically alleged and pleaded fraud in the plaint against the defendant-petitioner and others and, as such, the plaintiff needs an opportunity to prove the same by adducing evidence in the case. It cannot be rejected outright at the primary stage of the suit on an application under Order 7 rule 11 (d) of the Code. This submission of the learned Advocate finds support in the case reported in 50 DLR (AD) 99, wherein our Appellate Division has held that:</u>

<u>"The question of limitation in a suit is a mixed question of law and fact which can be decided only at the trial on taking evidence. In view of the relief prayed in the suit, the plaint cannot be rejected".</u>

<u>13. From the aforesaid discussions and decisions cited in the case as above, I do not find any substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner.</u>

<u>14. On the second leg of his submission, Mr Quayum vigorously argued that, the plaint ought to have been rejected by the trial Court finding that the same is barred by section 11 of the Code, that is, barred by the rule of res judicata. The learned Advocate submits that the fact and issue involved in the present suit have been directly and substantially in issue in the former suit between the same parties. He submits that if it appears from the reading of the plaint itself that the facts and issues involved in the suit were directly and substantially in issue in the former suit, the subsequent suit is not maintainable under the provisions of section 11 of the Code being barred by principle of res judicata. In elaborating his submission the learned Advocate took me to the averments made in the plaint and read out different paragraph of the same. It appears from the plaint at the present Title Suit No. 17 of 1998 that, there has been statements of some facts of the former suit being Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 on aforesaid auction sale, Bainanama, dakhalnama, etc in connection with Rent Suit No. 5 of 1932 and Money Execution Case No. 14 of 1933, etc. In view of such statements made in the plaint by the plaintiff, which have already been decided and disposed of in the former suit between the parties, the learned Advocate submits that, those cannot be tried in the subsequent suit as per provision of section 11 of the Code and so the plaint is liable to be rejected outright without going into evidence. In support of his submission he referred a decision of a case between Sreemati Pushpa Rani Das and another vs AKM Habibur Rahman and others, reported in 13 BLD (AD) 217. He also referred to decisions of the cases between Guinness Peat (Trading) Limited vs Md Fazlur Rahman, reported in 44 DLR (AD) 242, Shafiq Ahmed vs Mirza Muhammad Anwar Geb, reported in 20 DLR (WP) 113 and in the case between Habibullah and others vs SA Mujtaba and others, reported in 34 DLR 418. In the case of Sreemati Pushpa Rani Das and another vs AKM Habibur Rahman and others, reported in 13 BLD (AD) 217, it has been held by our Appellate Division that:</u>

<u>"The plea of res judicata is not available in rejecting a plaint under Order 7, rule 11 of the Civil Procedure Code. Whether the suit is barred by res judicata or not, is a matter to be decided at the time of trial, as raised by the defendants, and the same cannot be decided from a reading of the plaint. The maintainability of the suit on the ground of res judicata can very well be framed as an issue in the suit."</u>

<u>From reading of the aforesaid decision, I am of the opinion that this does not at all support the case of the defendant petitioner.</u>

<u>15. In the case between Guinness Peat (Trading) Limited vs Md Fazlur Rahman, reported in 44 DLR (AD) 242, wherein our Appellate Division held that:</u>

<u>"The plea of implied bar should ordinarily be decided on evidence unless the facts disclosed in the plaint clearly prove that the suit was not maintainable. A resort to section 151 of the Code may be made in an exceptional case.</u>

<u>It has been further held in the same case that:</u>

<u>"In an application for rejection of the plaint on the ground of non-disclosure of cause of action the Court need not dissect the plaintiff`s case part by part, if a part of the cause of action arises within its jurisdiction."</u>

<u>16. Since the learned Advocate for the  defendant-petitioner Mr Abdul Quayum did not at all urge before this Court the point under Order 7,  rule 11 (a) of the Code that, the suit shall be rejected because of non-disclosure of cause of action, I do not find that this decision has any application in the matter. Moreover, the present plaint has a clear disclosure of the cause of action.</u>

<u>In the other decision reported in 20 DLR (WP) 113, it has been held by the Lahore High Court that:</u>

<u>"Earlier suit filed for cancellation of sale deed on the ground that it is illegal and void-Latter suit for declaration that such deed was illegal and without consideration-Latter suit is bared under Order 1, rule 2(3)".</u>

<u>But the present case before us stands on different facts and footing in which the aforesaid decision has no manner of application at all.</u>

17. On the other hand, the learned Advocate Mr M A Wahhab Miah for the plaintiff-opposite party submits with reference to the averments made in the plaint and with reference to different Annexures vide Annexure C-F of the supplementary affidavit filed by the defendant-petitioner that, the two suits being Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 and Title Suit No. 17 of 1998 stand on a completely different footing. It may be mentioned here that the defendant-petitioner has not filed of enclosed the plaint of the earlier suit being Suit No. 45 of 1984:

From the judgment passed by the trial Court in said Title Suit No. 45 of the 1984 vide Annexure C it appears that the said suit was filed by the plaintiff opposite party for declaration of his title stating that:

“নালিশী জমি পাথরঘাটা মোজায় ৫৯নং খতিয়ানে ১২’৮৬ একর জমি বনী আমিন চোদ্দ আনা চার কড়া ও একক্রান্তি সত্য-----------------। কিন্তু উপরোক্ত জমির মধ্য মাত্র ৬২ শতাংশ জমি বনী আমিনের নামে রেকর্ড হয়। বাকী ১১’৯২ জমি অসুদ্ধভাবে ১-৮ নং নিবাদীর পূর্ববর্তীর ওয়াজেদ আলীর নামে অসুদ্ধভাবে রেকর্ড হয়।----------------; বিবাদীর ১৫ই কার্তিক ১৩৯০ সালে জমি দাবী করিয়াছে ১৬ আনা জমি তাহার স্বত্ব দখল করিতেছে”।

On such pleadings the plaintiff prayed for declaration of title in respect of share of their predecessor Bani Amin in the suit land in Title Suit No. 45 of 1984. In the aforesaid suit defendant Nos.3 and 10 filed written statements separately. In the said written statements it was stated by them that:

“বাদীগণের মোকদ্দমা বর্ণিত জমিতে কোন সত্ব দখল নাই। নালিশী জোত সাবেক বনি আমিন ও আরব আলীর সত্ব দখলেই ছিল। পিরজপুর ১ম মুনসেফী আদালতে ৫/৩২ ও ১৪/৩৩ নং টাকায় ও ডিক্রী জারীর মোকদ্দমায় নিলাম উঠিলে ১-৮ নং বিবাদীগণের পূর্ববর্তী ওয়াজেদ আলী জমাদ্দারন ৭-১০-৩৩ তাং নিলাম গুলো জোত খরিদ করে। উক্ত নিলাম ১০-১২-৩৩ তাং এ বহাল হয় অতপর তৎপর ২০-২-৩৪ তাং এ তিনি সরেজিমিনে দখল প্রাপ্ত হন”।

18. Referring the above, the learned Advocate Mr M A Wahhab Mia submits that, the, present plaintiff in the present Title Suit No.17 of 1998 has only and merely reproduced the said facts disclosed by the contesting defendant in Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 in their own written statements. The same was not stated by nor was the case of the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 nor any issue was framed on it or any evidence was led by the plaintiff on the same. He terms the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner as thoroughly misconceived and incorrect, submitting, that Mr Quayum has rather tried to level the case of the defendants set up in Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 as a case of the plaintiff which is untrue and incorrect.

<u>19. From reading of the plaint of the present suit as a whole and from reading of the judgment passed by the trial Court in Title Suit No. 45 of 1984 it clearly appears that the facts stated by the plaintiff in his plaint in Title Suit No. 17 of 1998 is nothing but a mere narration of the defence case of the defendant Nos. 3 and 10 of Title Suit No. 45 of 1984. It also appears from this judgment Annexure C that no issue was also framed on this fact. The present suit distinctly appears as a different one from the former suit; Moreover, the plaintiffs present suit is based on questioning the, genuineness of the Bainanama and Dakhalnama refiled before the High Court Division, in Civil Revision No. 732 of 1990. On the other hand, the former suit (TS No. 45 of 1984) was filed for declaration of his title alleging that there has been incorrect entry in the record of right in the name of the predecessor of the principal defendant late Wazed Ali Zamaddar in respect of suit land in PS Khatian No. 59 measuring 12.86, out of which only 62 decimals of land was recorded in his name. The heir of Bani Amin filed the said suit and there is absolutely no statement in the plaint of the former suit about the alleged rent suit, execution case, Bainanama, Dakhalnama etc. The statements in respect of rent suit, execution case, Bainanama, Dakhalnama, etc. had been made by the defendant Nos. 3 and 10 themselves in their written statements filed in the suit. The plaintiff has honestly stated the same in the plaint of his present suit only Therefore, it cannot be said that the issue involved in the former suit and in the present suit are directly and substantially the same between the same parties. It is clear that the present suit stands on different facts and footing with a totally different prayer and in such situation it cannot be said that the issues involved in the present suit have been directly and substantially in issue in the earlier suit and were adjudicated between the same parties. I therefore fail to agree with Mr Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate for the defendant petitioner that the suit is barred by res judicata and the plaint is liable to be rejected under Order 7, rule 11(d) of the Code. From my above discussions, findings and the authorities referred in the case, I hold that, both the question of limitation and of res judicata raised in the application under Order 7 rule 11(d) of the Code for rejecting the plaint of the present suit, are mixed questions of law and fact, which need thorough investigation on adequate evidence for arriving at a correct decision on framing specific issues by the trial Court. Here allegations to those effect in an application under Order 7 rule 11(d) of the Code is not sufficient compliance of the requirement of law for rejecting the plaint without affording the plaintiff an opportunity to defend and enforce his right to sue for an appropriate relief which he is otherwise entitled to get under the law.</u>

20. Mr Quayum also submitted that it would be embarrassing for the trial Court to try the suit on the same Bainanama and dakhalnama on the basis of which the superior Court of the country has already given their decision in favour of the defendant. But I have already discussed above that the present suit stands on different facts and prayer. Hence I find no substance in his submission. I have also already found that, the grounds taken by the defendant-petitioner in his application for rejecting the plaint under Order 7, rule 11 (d) of the Code on the ground of limitation and res judicata, being mixed question of law and facts, those cannot be decided on such an application under Order 7, rule 11(d) of the Code on mere reading of the plaint. The provisions of Order 7, rule 11 of the Code being a summary proceeding, such complicated questions of both facts and law, should not be allowed on such application and the Court must certainly be cautious and careful in granting such relief.

21. In view of my aforesaid discussions, observations and findings I am of the opinion that the trial Court has rightly rejected the application filed under Order 7, rule 11(a) and (d) of the Code by the defendant-petitioner. I find no merit in the Rule and the same is liable to be discharged.

22. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated.

23. The trial Court is hereby directed to disposes of the suit within 10 (ten) months from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment and order.

The office is hereby directed to send a copy of this judgment to the trial Court at the earliest.

End.
